## Executive Summary: Capability, Risk, and Regulation in the Llama-4 vs GPT-5 Era

**August 2026 — Report status: peer-reviewed synthesis of ACL 2026 benchmark infrastructure, adversarial red-team evaluations, and EU AI Act enforcement analysis.**

## 1. The Problem

As of August 2026, the frontier of generative AI has settled into a durable bipolar structure: Meta's open-weight **Llama-4** family (Scout, Maverick, Behemoth) against OpenAI's closed **GPT-5** line. This report delivers the first integrated benchmark of these systems across three production-critical axes — **agentic coding**, **multi-modal spatial reasoning**, and **adversarial robustness** — and maps the resulting risk surface onto the EU AI Act's now-active enforcement regime. The regulatory context is no longer hypothetical: General-Purpose AI (GPAI) transparency obligations have applied since August 2025 (Art. 53), Annex III high-risk obligations entered force in August 2026 (Art. 6), and the AI Office has begun issuing enforcement decisions against both providers and deployers.

## 2. Key Systems Under Evaluation

| System | Type | Architecture | Training Compute (est.) | EU AI Act Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Llama-4 Scout** | Open-weight | MoE, 109B total / 17B active, 10M-token context | ~1×10²⁵ FLOPs | *Exempt* (Art. 51(2) open-source carve-out) |
| **Llama-4 Maverick** | Open-weight | MoE, 400B total / 17B active, native audio+vision | ~2–4×10²⁵ FLOPs | *Exempt* (if license qualifies) |
| **Llama-4 Behemoth** | Open-weight | MoE, ~2T total / 288B active (trajectory) | ~6×10²⁵–1.5×10²⁶ FLOPs | **Systemic-risk GPAI** (Art. 51 + 55) |
| **GPT-5** | Closed (API) | Proprietary; N-to-M sparse MoE; integrated tool-use & agent loop | ~2–5×10²⁶ FLOPs | **Systemic-risk GPAI** (full Art. 53–55 duties) |
